clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse cares for a client wearing a halo brace after a cervical spine injury. Which nursing action is appropriate?

options.A: Provide ordered pin-site care and monitor for drainage, erythema, or evidence that a pin or the halo ring is loosening.
options.B: Leave the pin sites unassessed because infection and hardware loosening are not expected halo complications.
options.C: Retighten a loose halo pin independently whenever movement is noticed, without assessment by the spine team.
options.D: Remove a painful or draining pin at the bedside before obtaining a replacement or fixation plan.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current NCBI StatPearls guidance identifies pin-site infection and pin or halo-ring loosening as recognized complications of halo immobilization. It describes ongoing pin-site care and periodic clinician checks of pin torque as part of maintenance, with trained nursing staff carrying out ordered pin-site care and monitoring for complications. Persistent drainage may require clinician-directed antibiotic therapy or pin replacement. Therefore the nurse should perform prescribed care and surveillance and escalate concerns rather than independently retighten or remove fixation hardware.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Maintain halo safety through prescribed pin-site care and surveillance for infection or loosening while escalating fixation problems to appropriately trained clinicians.
semantic_correction.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Last updated March 2, 2024; StatPearls 2026 edition accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Maintenance/Complications — daily or alternate-day pin-site care; pin and halo-ring loosening and pin-site infection are recognized complications; persistent drainage/infection can require clinician-directed therapy or pin replacement. Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes — ordered pin-site care may be performed by trained nursing staff; spine-specialized clinician checks pin torque
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Halo management includes ongoing pin-site care and surveillance for pin-site infection and fixation loosening, with corrective pin tightening or replacement performed under appropriately trained clinician management.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, limited infection findings to directly supported drainage/erythema, and reserved pin tightening or replacement for appropriately trained clinician management.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests nursing surveillance and ordered pin-site care without authorizing independent manipulation of cervical fixation hardware.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches ongoing halo pin-site care and monitoring for infection or loosening.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Pin-site infection and pin/ring loosening are recognized halo complications.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Pin retorquing is a protocol-driven fixation procedure requiring appropriately trained clinician oversight.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Pin removal or replacement requires a clinician-directed plan that preserves cervical stabilization.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone preserves nursing surveillance and ordered care without unsafe fixation manipulation.
cueing_check: All four options are halo-care actions of comparable length and specificity; no unique-length or absolute-word cue identifies A.
